title: Change a click pen's refill: spring onto the new refill's tip, front barrel over both, then join it to the back half
instruction: Put the new refill in the pen: the spring onto its tip, the front barrel over them, then push the front barrel into the back half.
context: Changing a pen's refill is a familiar desk job. The small spring has to go onto the refill's tip, the front barrel over both, and then the refill and barrel, loose inside each other, have to be carried together, one hand on each, into the back half. A pen put together without its spring looks finished but doesn't click.
setup: Positions in cm from the midpoint between the arm bases: x forward, y to the robot's left; heights above the table top. A grey desk pen stand, fixed, centred at (30, -4): a 3 x 11 cm base, 4 mm thick, with three tubes 3 cm tall in a row, bores 7 mm at (30, -2), 12 mm at (30, -6) and 16 mm at (30, -10). In the 7 mm hole stands a new ballpoint refill point-up (11.5 cm long, 5 mm plastic ink tube, 2 mm front section 1.8 cm long with a brass point, 3 g). In the 12 mm hole stands the pen's blue front barrel nose-up (6 cm long, 10 mm across, 7 mm bore, 3 mm nose hole, 6 g). In the 16 mm hole stands the blue back half open end up (7 cm long, 14 mm across, 7 mm bore, 11.6 mm sleeve 8 mm deep at its open end, 7 g). The refill's steel spring (12 mm long, 5 mm across, 4 mm bore, 0.5 g) stands on end at (24, 6). Both arms start at the ready pose with open grippers. Nothing else is on the table.
scoring: Spring on the refill: its centre within 1.2 mm of the refill's axis, between 5 and 18 mm from the point. Front barrel over the refill: the refill's point within 1.5 mm of the barrel's axis, from 1 mm outside to 8 mm inside its nose, the two in line within 6 deg. Joined: the front barrel's open end within 1.5 mm of the back half's sleeve floor and axis, in line within 6 deg, the refill's end inside the back half. 1.0 (success): all three, both hands' tool points 4 cm from every part and no part moving over 1 cm/s, held 1 s; this ends the trial. Otherwise, at the end: 0.75 all three; 0.5 spring on and front barrel over; 0.25 spring on only; 0 if the spring is not on the refill, whatever else is done. Real trial: check the halves meet (gap under 1.5 mm, ruler) without moving the pen, then click it: the point comes out and goes back only with the spring on.
reset_notes: Nothing is used up: take the pen apart and stand the refill, front barrel and back half back in their holes and the spring on its mark.
fidelity: Rigid bodies of convex pieces, 240 Hz physics, 20 Hz control. The spring is a rigid tube (no compression) with a 4 mm bore, about 1 mm wider than a real pen spring's: with a real fit it jams on the refill in simulation. The halves push into a sleeve with 0.8 mm play instead of screwing together, and the click mechanism is left out (the refill rests on the back half's floor). Refill friction 0.25 (smooth plastic). The stand is fixed.
scores: Dream-1 run: 0.0 (2,400 steps; the arms moved to the stand, but the spring never went onto the refill); demo: 1.0 (1,172 steps, same in 3 runs). Steps 1-2 only (never joined): 0.5; the pen's parts handled without the spring: 0.
